item.description:
Beta release — thanks for testing.

Fixes

  • Speakers stay in the list. On some Wi-Fi networks a speaker could drop out of the list for a moment, or a stereo pair could briefly show as one of its halves. The app now asks speakers directly and remembers where they are, so every room shows up when the app opens and stays put.

Beta release — thanks for testing.

Fixes

  • Speakers no longer go missing. On some Wi-Fi networks the app could miss a speaker, or one half of a stereo pair, which then showed under its own name (like "HomePod Right") instead of the room. The app now checks for speakers it missed, so every room shows up.

Beta release — thanks for testing.

New

  • Pick speakers before you play. Tick rooms on the Speakers page while nothing is playing, and they join as soon as the music starts.
  • Install updates automatically. A new option in Settings › Updates downloads updates in the background. When one is ready, the app says so, with a button to restart now.
  • Play songs on HomePods paired with an Apple TV. If the Apple TV is waiting for Apple Music's latest privacy agreement, the app tells you to accept it there.

Fixes

  • New songs show right away. The app used to take up to 30 seconds to notice that the next song had started.
  • Next and back show that they're working, so it's clear the click landed.
  • Grouping speakers now uses the same request as Apple's own apps.
  • No more in-between steps when a room joins a group, and the song's time no longer jumps when a new song starts.
  • Keep stereo pairs ready for Home scenes (Settings › General): Apple's HomePod software can leave a stereo pair silent when a Home scene runs while the pair is still grouped with another room. This setting now ungroups 2 minutes after the music stops by default, and you can choose a longer time.
